parts.title: Part 1

passage.title: Emma's Adventure Across the Savanna
passage.content: Emma's dream was to travel across the African savanna. Early one morning, she arrived at a wide _____ full of golden grass and tall trees. As Emma walked, she saw herds of zebras grazing quietly. The black and white stripes of the _____ looked beautiful against the yellow grass. Nearby, a group of elephants was moving slowly across the savanna. Emma watched the _____ use their trunks to pull leaves from the trees. Later, Emma decided to explore a small lake by renting a boat. She gently sailed the _____ across the calm water, feeling the warm breeze. At night, Emma sat outside her camp, looking up at the sky filled with bright stars. The _____ over the savanna were clearer and closer than she had ever seen before. When she felt hungry, Emma visited a cozy local restaurant. There, she tasted traditional African dishes, full of spices and fresh ingredients. At the end of her trip, Emma boarded a small train that crossed the savanna. As the _____ moved through the grasslands, Emma watched the zebras, elephants, and endless beauty of the land disappear into the distance.

questions.hint: a wide _____ full of golden grass
The _____ over the savanna were clearer
As the _____ moved through the grasslands

parts.instruction: Read the text. Fill in each gap with ONE word. You must use a word which is somewhere in the rest of the text.

q1.text: The passage begins by stating Emma's dream was to visit the African savanna. The gap describes the wide area with golden grass where she arrived. That's why the correct answer is 'savanna'.
q1.quote: Emma's dream was to travel across the African savanna.

q2.text: The sentence just before the gap mentions that Emma saw herds of zebras. The gapped sentence then describes their characteristic black and white stripes. That's why the correct answer is 'zebras'.
q2.quote: As Emma walked, she saw herds of zebras grazing quietly.

q3.text: The text first mentions a group of elephants. The following sentence describes watching these animals use their trunks to get leaves, which is a unique behavior of elephants. That's why the correct answer is 'elephants'.
q3.quote: Nearby, a group of elephants was moving slowly across the savanna.

q4.text: The previous sentence states that Emma rented a boat to explore a lake. The gapped sentence describes her sailing this object across the calm water. That's why the correct answer is 'boat'.
q4.quote: Later, Emma decided to explore a small lake by renting a boat.

q5.text: The sentence before the gap says Emma was looking at the night sky, which was 'filled with bright stars'. The gapped sentence then comments on how clear these were. That's why the correct answer is 'stars'.
q5.quote: At night, Emma sat outside her camp, looking up at the sky filled with bright stars.

q6.text: The previous sentence explains that Emma boarded a small train for the end of her trip. The gapped sentence describes this vehicle moving through the grasslands. That's why the correct answer is 'train'.
q6.quote: At the end of her trip, Emma boarded a small train that crossed the savanna.

parts.title: Part 3

paragraphs.content: Short visual clips and rapid storytelling have become a dominant form of creative expression online. Artists now work within limited time frames, often just a few seconds, to convey emotions or ideas to wide audiences. This compressed format challenges traditional forms of art, requiring speed, simplicity, and instant connection to the viewer.

Many individuals who once shared their artistic hobbies casually now depend on their creative work for a living. Through clever self-promotion and audience engagement, they secure financial support, brand partnerships, and product sales. However, sustaining a long-term career demands constant innovation, strategic thinking, and personal branding beyond pure artistic talent.

Learning creative skills used to require enrolling in expensive schools or relocating to artistic hubs. Today, anyone with an internet connection can join expert-led classes, gaining the technical knowledge needed to improve their craft. This shift has allowed aspiring creators from all over the world to access opportunities that were once geographically or financially out of reach.

Working together across countries has become effortless for today's artists. Musicians, filmmakers, and designers collaborate in real-time without ever meeting face-to-face. This has not only expanded access to global perspectives but also introduced fresh ideas by blending diverse cultural backgrounds into new works.

The success of a creative project online often depends less on quality and more on invisible digital patterns. These complex systems prioritize some works over others based on hidden criteria like user preferences and activity history. As a result, gaining visibility today requires not just creativity, but also an understanding of how online exposure really works.

Sharing art across online platforms brings significant risks for creators. Ideas, designs, and original works can easily be copied or redistributed without permission. As a result, modern artists must find ways to safeguard their intellectual property, using technological tools and legal strategies to defend their ownership rights.

Short-Form Creativity in the Digital Era
The Growing Importance of Intellectual Property

parts.title: Part 4

passage.title: Genetically Modified Foods
passage.content:
The development of genetically modified (GM) foods has been one of the most significant scientific advances in agriculture over the past few decades. By altering the genetic structure of plants and animals, scientists have created new varieties that are resistant to pests, diseases, and extreme weather conditions. Supporters argue that GM foods have the potential to enhance food security, reduce the environmental impact of farming, and improve nutritional content for populations around the world.

One of the primary motivations behind genetic modification is to increase crop yields. Traditional farming methods are often vulnerable to factors such as drought, insects, and plant diseases, which can significantly reduce harvests. By introducing specific genes into crops like corn, soybeans, and rice, scientists have developed strains that can survive harsh conditions and require fewer chemical treatments. This, in turn, can lead to lower costs for farmers and a reduction in the use of pesticides and herbicides, benefiting both human health and the environment.

Advocates also highlight the potential of GM foods to address nutritional deficiencies. For instance, "Golden Rice" has been engineered to contain higher levels of Vitamin A, aiming to combat deficiencies in regions where malnutrition remains a severe problem. Proponents believe that biofortified crops like these could play a crucial role in reducing global health inequalities and improving the quality of life in developing countries.

Despite these potential advantages, the use of GM technology in food production remains highly controversial. Critics argue that not enough is known about the long-term health effects of consuming genetically modified organisms (GMOs). Although numerous scientific studies have found no conclusive evidence that GM foods are harmful, public skepticism persists, fueled by concerns about the influence of large biotechnology corporations and the perceived unnaturalness of genetic modification.

Environmental concerns are another area of debate. Some researchers worry that GM crops could crossbreed with wild plants, leading to unintended ecological consequences such as the creation of "superweeds" that are resistant to conventional herbicides. Others raise ethical questions about the patenting of living organisms and the potential monopolization of the global food supply by a small number of powerful companies.

The issue of labeling GM foods has sparked further controversy. In many countries, consumers demand the right to know whether the products they purchase contain genetically modified ingredients. However, labeling regulations vary widely across different regions. While the European Union mandates clear labeling of GM products, other regions, including parts of North America, have more flexible policies, leading to confusion and debate over consumer rights and transparency.

As scientific innovation continues to advance, the future of GM foods will depend on balancing technological possibilities with ethical considerations, environmental protection, and public trust. Greater investment in independent research, open dialogue between stakeholders, and comprehensive regulatory frameworks may help address concerns and ensure that the benefits of genetic modification are realized in a responsible and sustainable manner.

passage.title: Volunteering
passage.content:
For almost every person there will be a time in their life when they decide that they want to volunteer. There could be numerous reasons why you want to start doing volunteering work - from retirement to plain old fashioned good will. Different people may find different arguments in favour of doing this kind of work or service, if I can put it this way. But how do you get into the world of volunteering?

First of all, you need to make time to volunteer and before you can start approaching organizations and enquiring about volunteering opportunities, you need to first figure out how much of your time you can dedicate to volunteering. If you are working, then ask your employer if you can have consistent weekdays off, so you can then have regular time to volunteer each week. When you can promise a set amount of time to an organization, then they are much more likely to offer you a volunteering position. So think twice whether you can allocate enough time to this work before you start, otherwise it can be very disappointing for both sides. Next, it is time to think about why you want to volunteer. This may sound obvious, but have a good long think about the reasons why you are volunteering. Is it because you're passionate about helping others? Is it because you want to meet and spend time with new people? Or is it because you want to gain further experience and qualifications? Knowing your motives can help you decide which organizations and roles are best suited to your wants. Mind there are more opportunities for volunteering than you might know about or imagine.

The next step is to find an organization to volunteer with. You can volunteer at a local homeless shelter or at a charity shop. Maybe you like working with children, in which case the local youth center would be an ideal place to start with. Perhaps animals are more your thing, so you could ask a local animal shelter if they need a hand. As it was mentioned before, there are plenty of places you could volunteer to work with. Simply do your research, find the place that suits you and get in touch. Many organizations don't advertise that they're looking for volunteers, so it may be up to you to make the first move and contact them.

So, now you know how much time you can dedicate to volunteering, as well as why you want to volunteer and where you want to do it. The next step is to secure your position working within that organization by writing a CV. This may not be a paid position, but that doesn't mean you should be less ambitious than you normally would be when approaching a potential employer. In your CV you should outline any experience you've had that is relevant to your voluntary position, explain why you want to volunteer and how you would benefit the company. State clearly how much free time you have to dedicate and how long you would be comfortable to work for the organization in terms of days, weeks, and months.

Laying out these clear ground rules will prevent you from being taken advantage of and overworked, and will also help your potential employer understand your needs. Apart from being rewarding in many ways (though not in the financial one), volunteering is often envisaged as an important part of social and personal maturing. No wonder there are so many volunteers among the young people in many countries of the world.
